match.reason: No point in the bank covers types of markets such as resource, industrial, consumer, mass or niche; the closest, on customers, suppliers and competitors, is a related but different idea.

draft.title: Types of markets
card: sells raw materials and other inputs, such as timber, minerals or labour, to businesses that use them to make things.
businesses buy goods and services to use in making other products or running the business, such as machinery or cleaning services.
resellers, such as wholesalers and retailers, buy finished goods to sell on to others at a profit.

individuals and households buy goods and services for their own use. A mass market sells one product to a very large, broad group of buyers. A niche market targets a small, specific group with particular needs.
draft.remember: Each market is defined by who buys and why, so each needs its own marketing approach.

a.q: Which buyer is part of the intermediate market?
opts: A wholesaler buying stock to sell to shops
A family buying a fridge for their home
A sawmill buying logs to cut into timber
A factory buying a new machine to use in production
a.why: An intermediate market is made up of resellers who buy finished goods to sell on. The factory buying a machine is in the industrial market, because it uses the machine itself and does not resell it.
a.clue: Which buyer plans to sell the goods on?

b.q: Priya runs a small online shop in Hobart that sells only gluten-free baking mixes to people with coeliac disease. Which type of market does she mainly serve?
opts: A niche market
A mass market
An industrial market
A resource market
b.why: Priya targets a small, specific group with particular needs, which is a niche market. A mass market is the tempting wrong answer, because she sells to consumers, but a mass market aims at a very large, broad group and not a small one.
b.clue: Think about how small and specific her group of buyers is.

a.best: A wholesaler buying stock to sell to shops

problems.detail: The remember line says each market is defined by who buys and why, but the card defines the resource market by what is sold, and mass and niche markets by the size and breadth of the target group, not by who buys or why. The remember line sorts the ideas more neatly than the card does.

Mass and niche markets sit inside the consumer market bullet. This suggests they are kinds of consumer market, when the syllabus lists them as separate market types and they can apply to business buyers too. They would be clearer as their own bullet.

proposal.title: Types of markets
card: A resource market sells raw materials and other inputs, such as timber, minerals or labour. In an industrial market, businesses buy goods or services to make products or run the business, such as machinery.
In an intermediate market, resellers such as wholesalers and retailers buy finished goods to sell on to others at a profit.
In a consumer market, individuals and households buy goods and services for their own use. Each type of market needs its own marketing approach.
Mass and niche markets differ in how wide the target group is. A mass market aims at a very large, broad group, while a niche market targets a small, specific group with particular needs.
